text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm very sorry about your dad. Yes, I'll help. Before we talk about any plans, I'd like to understand what matters to you. When you say you won't sign off on a "family discount," what is that protecting for you, and why does it matter? You also mentioned B could use money. Is that a concern of yours, or something B has said? Any concern counts, even a small one.

Thanks. I want my fair share, and I’m not agreeing to subsidize A by selling her the house cheaply. I don’t know what B has said about needing money, so I can’t speak for her. I want this settled fairly, but there’s no rush.

Hello. I'm very sorry about your father. C asked me to help the family work through the will and the house. I'm not here to push any outcome, and I can't make legal decisions or move money. I'd like to hear what matters to you about the house and why. I understand you and your husband may want to buy it. What makes that important to you? Any concern is welcome, even a small one.

Thank you. My husband and I want to buy the house at a family discount. Having a home we can afford matters to me, and I want to be financially independent. But C’s agreement is needed, and she hasn’t agreed.

Hello. I'm very sorry about your father. C asked me to help the family work through the will and the house. I'm not here to push any outcome, and I can't make legal decisions or move money. I'd like to hear from you directly: what matters to you about the house and the estate, and why? Please share any concern, even a small one. It counts as much as anyone else's.

Thank you. I don’t have a particular wish to keep the house, but I’d like the estate handled fairly and not rushed. If there’s money available to me, I’d hope to use it to start a dance studio; I’m not sure what amount or share is possible.

Thank you. Here's how I'd put what matters to you. Please tell me if it fits or needs changing: "C wants the estate divided in a way that is fair and that she can see is fair, with each sister receiving her rightful share, and with time to settle it properly." Have I missed or misstated anything, even slightly?
Mostly. I do want a fair share, and there’s no rush. But “rightful share” isn’t settled, and it matters that I haven’t agreed to a discounted sale to A.

Thank you. Here's how I'd put what matters to you. Please correct it if it doesn't fit: "A wants a secure home she and her husband can afford, and to be financially independent." I've left out the specific discount for now so we can first agree on the underlying need. Is there anything else? For example, does the house itself matter to you beyond the cost, such as memories or the location?
That mostly fits. The family discount matters because it affects whether we can afford to buy it. I’m not sure I have more to add about memories or location.

Thank you. Here's how I'd put what matters to you. Please correct it if it doesn't fit: "B wants the estate handled fairly and without rushing, and wants clarity on what her share could be, so she can plan toward starting her dance studio." Is that right? Is anything missing, even something small?
Yes, that’s right. I’d only add that I’d like my share to give me a little more independence, if that’s possible.

Thank you, that helps. Revised wording: "C wants the estate divided in a way she can see is fair, with how each share is defined worked out openly and agreed rather than assumed, and with nothing settled without her consent and no time pressure." Does this fit? Also, do you know what the will says about how the estate is divided, and who the executor is? I'm asking for the facts only, not to pick a side.
Mostly. I haven’t agreed to A buying at a discount; I can’t say that every estate decision needs my consent. I don’t know what the will says or who the executor is.

Thanks. Updated wording: "A wants a secure home she and her husband can afford, and to be financially independent. Affordability is a key factor in whether owning the house is realistic for her." Does that fit? I'll be honest that C has said she won't agree to a discounted price. So it may help to look at several ways to make it affordable, for example a mortgage against your share, paying the others over time, or other routes. Would you be open to exploring those? It's completely fine to say no or to raise any discomfort.

Yes, that fits. I’m open to exploring options, but I’d need to understand the costs and whether they’d leave me financially secure before agreeing to anything. I still hope we can find a price that works for the family.

Understood, I went too far there. Revised: "C wants the estate divided in a way she can see is fair, with how shares are defined worked out openly rather than assumed, and with enough time to do it properly." Does that fit now? One concern of my own I'd like to check with you: I want any plan to rest on clear facts, meaning what the will actually says, who the executor is, and an independent valuation of the house, before anyone commits to anything. Does that sit okay with you?
Yes, that fits. And yes, I’m fine with checking the will, executor, and an independent house valuation before anyone commits. There’s no rush.

Thank you. Recorded as: "B wants the estate handled fairly and without rushing, with clarity on her share, and wants that share to give her more independence, such as toward a dance studio." My own concern, which I'd like to check with you: any plan should rest on clear facts first, meaning what the will says, who the executor is, and an independent valuation of the house. Do you know what the will says or who the executor is? Any discomfort with that approach?
I’m afraid I don’t know what the will says or who the executor is. Getting those facts and an independent valuation first sounds sensible to me.

Thank you, recorded. My own concern, which I'd like to check with you: plans should rest on clear facts first (the will, the executor, an independent valuation). Here's a draft first step for everyone: (1) find the will and the executor; (2) get an independent valuation; (3) you get finance quotes so you can see what buying would cost you and whether you'd stay secure. No one commits to anything, and the question of price stays open, recorded honestly as unresolved between you and C. Does anything in this make you uncomfortable, even slightly?
No, that seems sensible. I’d just want to keep my finance details private unless I choose to share them.

Draft first step for all three of you: (1) find the will and the executor; (2) get an independent valuation; (3) A looks into finance options so the family can see what's realistic for her; (4) B gets clarity on her likely share. Nobody commits to anything, and the discount question is recorded as unresolved, not agreed. Does anything here bother you, even a little?
The fact-finding is fine, as long as A exploring finance doesn’t imply I’ll accept a discount or cover any shortfall. B’s likely share should be clarified from the will and the facts, not guessed.

Draft first step for all three of you: (1) find the will and the executor; (2) get an independent valuation; (3) A looks into finance options; (4) once the facts are known, you get a clear figure for your likely share so you can plan the studio. Nobody commits to anything yet. Does anything here bother you, even a little?
That seems sensible, as long as the figure for my share is only an estimate until the will and other details are clear. I’d also hope nobody feels committed just because A looks into financing.
